title: Grateful Dead Live at The Matrix on 1966-11-29

ai_review.summary: Soundboard capture of an early‑1966 show with raw, vinyl‑like grit but plenty of feverish psychedelic R&B and standout early songs
ai_review.review: The recording is a soundboard source that isn’t pristine – listeners note channel drop‑outs and a lo‑fi, vinyl‑style hiss – yet it conveys the wild energy of the Dead’s November 1966 Matrix gig. The performance features rare early cuts (Big Boy Pete, Been Down So Long, Same Thing) and a soaring Early Morning Rain, with a tight bebop‑flavored drum intro and an exhilarating closing jam.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers give 5‑star praise for the show’s energy and rare material; a few note recording flaws, pulling the overall weighted rating to around 4.2

recording_quality.technical_notes: Lo‑fi, vinyl‑like hiss and occasional channel drop‑out (e.g., during Viola Lee); not crystal clear but captures the live ambience; some reviewers call it "bad recording" yet still enjoyable

standout_songs: I Just Want To Make Love To You
show_quality.setlist_flow: Three‑set early show mixing blues standards and fledgling originals; rare cuts appear throughout, ending with an uplifting jam that leaves a strong impression.

band_member_comments.Drums: Kreutzmann opens the set on a bebop‑style drum figure, noted as a highlight by reviewers.
